Cyclone Akvan to make landfall between Nellore and Tuni in Andhra as very severe storm on November 20
 Andhra fishermen, still awaiting compensation for Cyclone Arnab’s losses, are told to stay ashore till November 20
 Updated - November 16, 2026 10:34 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA 
 Nellore Sravani, V. Kamalakara Rao READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 A satellite image of the deep depression over the Bay of Bengal on Monday. The system is likely to intensify into Cyclone Akvan and cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Tuni by noon on November 20.
 | Photo Credit: IMD
 Cyclone Akvan, expected to form over the Bay of Bengal on Monday evening, is very likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni by noon on November 20 as a very severe cyclonic storm , the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in its forecast on Monday (November 16, 2026). Winds at landfall may reach 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph.
 That leaves about 500 km of coast in play, that is, nearly half of Andhra Pradesh’s 1,053-km shoreline. Machilipatnam sits roughly in the middle. Weather experts are monitoring the system as it may change its course again.
 The Deep Depression over Southeast & adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 06 kmph during past 06 hours and lay centered at 0830 hours IST of today, the 16th November, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 11.2°N and Longitude 86.4°E, about 630 km east-northeast of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka), 690 km west of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman & Nicobar Islands), 700 km east-southeast of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 800 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 910 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha).
It is very likely to continue to move north-northwestwards, intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm over the central parts of south & adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal in the evening of today, the 16th November and into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal in the evening of 17th November, 2026. Thereafter, it is likely to intensify further and move west-northwestwards and cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni, by noon of 20th November, 2026 as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph.
— India Meteorological Department (@Indiametdept) November 16, 2026 Initial forecasts had indicated that the system may move towards north coastal Andhra Pradesh . The latest IMD bulletin places its landfall in central and south coastal Andhra Pradesh.
 Previously, very severe cyclonic storm Arnab made landfall near Narsapur, part of central Andhra Pradesh, and severe cyclonic storm Murasu near Ongole in south coastal Andhra Pradesh.
 Cyclone Akvan to hit Andhra on November 20; Naidu reviews preparedness, 173 fishing boats yet to return Krishna district, of which Machilipatnam is a part, has seen devastating cyclones in the past, including the infamous 1977 Diviseema cyclone . However, the district was spared much of the damage during Arnab and Murasu.
 బంగాళాఖాతంలో తీవ్రవాయుగుండం ప్రస్తుతానికి చెన్నైకు700 కి.మీ., విశాఖపట్నంకు800 కి.మీ.,గోపాల్‌పూర్ కు 910కి.మీ దూరంలో కేంద్రీకృతమై ఉంది.
సాయంత్రానికి తుపానుగా, రేపు తీవ్రతుపానుగా మారే అవకాశం ఉంది.
#Akvan #Cyclone #AndhraPradesh #APSDMA #RTGS #WeatherUpdate #weather #WeatherUpdate https://t.co/itmX4gtEiV
— Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (@APSDMA) November 16, 2026 Meanwhile, the depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal concentrated into a deep depression over the southeast and southwest Bay of Bengal in the early hours of Monday (November 16, 2026). The system moved north-northwestwards at 6 kmph during the past six hours, and at 8.30 a.m., it lay centred about 630 km east-northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 690 km west of Sri Vijaya Puram in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, 700 km east-southeast of Chennai in Tamil Nadu , 800 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and 910 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha .
 Odisha orders early evacuation of vulnerable areas as cyclone threat looms The system is very likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of the south and west-central Bay of Bengal by Monday evening, and into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by Tuesday evening (November 17). It is then likely to intensify further and move west-northwestwards towards the coast.
 Squally weather, with wind speeds touching 50-60 kmph, may begin along the coast from Monday. It is likely to increase gradually, becoming a gale as the system intensifies further. Sea conditions are very likely to be rough to very rough till November 17, after which they will worsen, the IMD said.
 Pre-cyclone watch
 The IMD has issued a pre-cyclone watch for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts. Moving north-northwestward at 8 kmph, the system is projected to reach near the Andhra Pradesh coast around the night of November 19 as a very severe cyclonic storm.
 Very severe cyclonic storm ‘Arnab’ begins landfall near Narsapur; Vizag battered by rain “The current atmospheric steering points towards the coastal stretch between north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha. It is too early to predict the landfall point of the storm,” a meteorologist told The Hindu. 
 District administrations have been placed on high alert and have advised a complete suspension of offshore operations.
 Fishermen told to stay ashore till November 20
 Fishermen have been told not to venture into the sea until November 20. Fishermen’s leader Arjili Dasu said the recurring weather disruptions had crippled livelihoods during Karteeka Masam, when fish sales already slump.
 Fisheries Joint Director L.B.S. Vardhan said Cyclone Arnab caused damage worth ₹307 lakh to fisheries in Visakhapatnam district: ₹123 lakh in partial damage and ₹184 lakh in full damage. No damage was recorded during Cyclone Murasu.
 “We have submitted our assessment reports to the higher-ups. We are awaiting their decision regarding the compensation payment,” Mr. Vardhan told The Hindu on Monday.
